caption:
AI stocks crashed on Thursday. By 11 a.m. New York time the Nasdaq was down 5% and the S&P 500 down 3.2%, AP reported.
Nvidia fell 8.3%, AMD 15.9% and CoreWeave 14.9%.
Investors fear the midterm results could slow the building of new AI data centers.

Is this a dip or the start of the AI bubble popping?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

threads_text: AI stocks got hammered on Thursday: the Nasdaq was down 5% by late morning and Nvidia lost 8.3%, AP reported. Investors fear new limits on data center construction after the midterms. Dip to buy or the start of the AI bubble popping?

paragraphs.text: Shares of companies tied to the artificial intelligence buildout fell sharply on Thursday, November 5, 2026. By 11 a.m. Eastern time, the S&P 500 was down 3.2%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average had lost 1,146 points, or 2.1%, and the Nasdaq composite was down 5%, according to the Associated Press. The S&P 500 was on track for its worst day since April 2025.

The drop erased the gains from Wednesday, November 4, when the market had its best session in three months, the AP reported. Reuters said the Nasdaq 100 was on track to lose about $1.8 trillion in stock market value and that the Nasdaq composite was heading toward a correction, a fall of 10% from its recent peak.
Chipmakers and cloud providers fall hardest

Nvidia fell 8.3% by late morning, after a 3.2% decline the day before, and was the heaviest drag on the S&P 500, according to the AP. Advanced Micro Devices dropped 15.9% and CoreWeave, which rents out AI computing power, fell 14.9%. GE Vernova, which makes power equipment, lost 9.1%.

Reuters reported that the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index fell 10.2% to its lowest level in more than six months, weighed down by Nvidia and Broadcom. Nebius dropped 15.2%, and Applied Digital, Cipher Digital and IREN each fell more than 18%. CoreWeave's five-year credit default spreads widened to a record, according to Reuters. Amazon fell 3.9% and Alphabet 2.7%.

The sell-off was not limited to the United States. South Korea's Kospi index fell 5.3% on Thursday, with Samsung Electronics down 7.6% and SK Hynix down 9.4%, the AP reported. In Japan, Tokyo Electron lost 9.5% and Advantest 15%.

The AP said investors are concerned that construction of AI data centers could slow because borrowing has become expensive. Democratic gains in the midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3, also raised the possibility that governments could pause new data center construction, which would reduce purchases of AI chips.

Reuters reported that investors worry Democratic control of Congress could bring tougher scrutiny of data centers at a time of growing local opposition to new facilities. UBS analysts estimated that around 30% of the US data center capacity additions expected in 2028 could be at risk from construction pauses. Investors are also increasingly questioning whether heavy spending on AI will pay off, according to Reuters.

Not every stock fell. AppLovin, which uses AI in its advertising business, rose 30.2% after beating revenue and profit expectations and approving a buyback of up to $3.2 billion, the AP reported. About two in five stocks in the S&P 500 were higher.

The day showed how closely the AI trade now depends on physical construction. Chip demand rests on data centers being built, and those projects need cheap financing, power and local permission. A political shift that touches any of those inputs now moves the most valuable companies in the market.
The next signal is whether newly elected officials and local governments actually move to pause data center projects, and whether chipmakers' coming earnings show any slowdown in orders.
